headline: Lets Secret Service protective employees keep earning overtime and other premium pay above the normal federal pay cap through 2028.
what_it_does: Federal law normally caps how much Secret Service protective employees can earn in a year. This law extends, through 2028, an exception that lets them receive overtime and other premium pay even if it pushes their yearly pay over that cap. Employees who do routine administrative or technical work are not covered. The Secret Service must also send Congress reports on overtime use, pay above the cap, and plans to reduce overtime, such as hiring more staff and spreading out the workload.

who_it_affects.how: They can be paid for overtime and other premium work even when it raises their total yearly pay above the usual federal limit.

who_it_affects.group: Secret Service administrative and technical staff
who_it_affects.how: They are not eligible for premium pay above the cap under this law.
It must report to Congress within 180 days on staffing demand and ways to cut overtime, and give regular reports on pay above the cap through 2027.

when_it_takes_effect: Treated as taking effect December 31, 2023 (enacted February 6, 2024); the pay exception runs through 2028. First pay-data report due within 30 days of enactment, and the staffing report within 180 days.
